newsitem.title: JAPAN: SANYO SEC SEES INSURERS ACCEPTING REPAYMENT DELAY.
newsitem.headline: SANYO SEC SEES INSURERS ACCEPTING REPAYMENT DELAY.

text.p: Sanyo Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday that it believes that a request it has made to life insurers for a delay in repayment of subordinated loans will be accepted.
"We think that our request will be accepted," said a Sanyo spokesman.

The medium-sized brokerage received loans from major life insurance companies, such as Nippon Life Insurance Co and Dai-Ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co, in a bid to increase its capital and strengthen its financial status.
The loans, worth 20 billion yen, come due at the end of July 1998.
However, subordinated loans cease to be counted as capital once the remaining period to maturity falls below one year. At that point, such loans are treated as short-term debt.
Sanyo said on Wednesday that it was asking the life insurers to extend the maturity of the subordinated loans.
Sanyo has been having financial trouble because of bad-loan problems at its affiliates, including a nonbank finance company.
The Sanyo spokesman also said that the brokerage does not expect to alter a nine-year restructuring programme it had started in the 1994/95 business year.
"The purpose of requesting an extension of loan terms from the insurers is to maintain our nine-year programme," said the spokesman.
He said the company has been considering various measures to restructure further, including one that would have it move its branches to where rents are cheaper.
